title: Turbo Mode: instruction-set rendering instead of pixel streaming, and what the endpoint needs

prose.text: Turbo Mode changes how Cloud Browser delivers the rendered page, not what runs where. {{instruction-set}} {{no-local-code}}

prose.label: Where it is set.
prose.text: {{per-profile}} The preconfigured Miscellaneous & Unknown profile has it on: [[zbi.misc-unknown-subscription:fixed-settings]]. What a user on an unsupported browser gets from a profile with Turbo Mode on is open {{gap:unsupported-fallback}}.

checks.do: Whether Turbo Mode is enabled in the isolation profile the user's rule names.
Whether the endpoint has hardware acceleration with WebGL and WebGL2, and is not Internet Explorer 11.

instruction-set.statement: Turbo Mode is an alternative to pixel streaming that transfers rendered information from the isolated browser to the local browser as an instruction set; Zscaler describes it as much faster and much less bandwidth intensive than pixel streaming.

quotes: Turbo Mode is an alternative to pixel streaming. It allows the transfer of rendered information from an isolated browser to a local browser as an instruction set.
This method of rendering is much faster and much less bandwidth intensive than pixel streaming.

no-local-code.statement: Enabling Turbo Mode on an isolation profile does not change security: web content is still processed on isolation containers, only rendered content reaches the user's browser, and no code is executed locally on the device.

quotes: There is no compromise to security if you enable Turbo Mode on an isolation profile.
Web content is processed on isolation containers, and only the rendered content appears in the end user's browser. As a result, no code is executed locally on the device.

requirements.statement: Turbo Mode needs hardware acceleration enabled on the user's device with WebGL and WebGL2 support, and it is not supported for Internet Explorer 11.

quotes: The user's device must have hardware acceleration enabled, with support for WebGL and WebGL2, in order to utilize Turbo Mode.
Turbo Mode is not supported for Internet Explorer 11.

modern-devices.statement: Turbo Mode is fully functional on most modern desktops and mobile devices.

quotes: Turbo Mode is fully functional on most modern desktops and mobile devices.

benefits.statement: With Turbo Mode, web content renders at up to 50 frames per second, and rendering instructions are cached so that scrolling a page transfers minimal to no additional data.

quotes: Rendering of web content at up to 50 frames per second.
Caching of rendering instructions, which facilitates faster scrolling of a web page with the transfer of minimal to no additional data.

per-profile.statement: Admins must enable Turbo Mode in the user's isolation profile, for Internet & SaaS and for Private Access profiles alike.

quotes: Admins must enable this feature in the user's isolation profile.
To learn more, see Creating Isolation Profiles for Internet & SaaS and Creating Isolation Profiles for Private Access.

unsupported-fallback.title: What a profile with Turbo Mode on does for a browser that cannot use it
unsupported-fallback.detail: Unverified legacy statement: Turbo Mode is default-on-if-supported, and pixel streaming serves Internet Explorer 11 and WebGL-disabled endpoints. The capture says admins must enable Turbo Mode per profile and lists its requirements, but not whether an unsupported browser falls back to pixel streaming or fails.
unsupported-fallback.blocks: predicting the experience of a user without WebGL2 or hardware acceleration on a Turbo Mode profile
